concept.name: Standard deviation channel
concept.definition: A channel built on a least-squares linear regression line through the last n closes, with parallel upper and lower lines plotted a set number of standard deviations (typically 2) of price away from the regression line.
concept.intuition: The regression line is the best-fit trend through the window and the bands mark statistically typical deviation around it - about two-thirds of observations within +/-1 sigma if deviations were normal.
concept.mechanics: Fit y = a + mx to the last n closes by least squares, compute the standard deviation of closes over the window, and plot the regression line with parallel lines offset by +/-k sigma (k = 2 default). The slope gives trend direction and the width gives volatility; it generates no signals by itself.
concept.formula: Center: y(x) = a + mx from the least-squares fit over n bars; Upper = y + k x sigma, Lower = y - k x sigma, sigma = standard deviation of the n closes, k typically 2.
concept.failure_modes: The channel is refit every bar, so historical channel lines repaint and backtests on drawn channels are unreliable; the symmetric deviation assumption fails in trending or fat-tailed markets.
concept.misconceptions: Unlike Bollinger Bands the center is a regression line, not a moving average, and price does not owe a return to it - in strong trends price rides one side of the channel.
concept.example: A 40-bar regression of closes gives y = 98 + 0.1x with sigma = 1.2; at the last bar the center is 102, the 2-sigma upper band 104.4 and the lower 99.6.
